name: Hybrid noise+distortion layer separate from sub/harmonic patch
goal: Build a portable hybrid stack: one patch/layer for filtered noise through asymmetric distortion (gritty air/texture) with EQ low-cut and slight top trim, and a separate patch/layer for sub/harmonic tones (e.g. square/WT) so you can retune harmonics or hold a fixed noise pitch without the noise timbre tracking every bass note—then blend; maps to sample/noise + WT + filter hybrid thinking for cinematic beds (not only neuro bass).
prerequisites: Synth with noise source (or noise osc), filter, distortion/waveshape, EQ; ability to run two instances or two layers

inputs.name: noise_color
inputs.description: Noise type / table (transcript likes AC-hum-style noise)

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Source is neuro-bass oriented; for cinematic pads keep distortion/filter milder and use the same split-layer principle (noise texture ≠ harmonic engine).

steps.action: Layer A (noise texture): start from a sine (or muted tonal osc), enable noise oscillator/source; set noise level ~50% and adjust noise pitch (~55% in source) to taste.
Add asymmetric (or similar) distortion ~50% to grit the noise. Filter the noise path (source ~cutoff example in mid-high range) to pull harshness back.

EQ the noise layer: high-pass/roll off the bottom (Q ~45% to flatten a hump), set HP frequency into the low-mid region so the noise isn’t muddy; optionally trim highs ~−2.5 dB. Mute the tonal osc on this layer if sub will be separate.

Layer B (harmonics/sub): separate instance/patch for low tones so changing WT/harmonics won’t rewrite the noise timbre. Prefer a harmonically useful wave (transcript favors square) or WT; shape independently.

Performance trick: hold one noise-layer pitch across moving sub notes so grit stays consistent while bass harmony moves—or map both together if you want noise to track. Blend to taste; for pads, lower distortion and lengthen amps, still keeping noise and WT/filter on independent paths.
steps.expect: Hybrid stack with independent noise vs harmonic control

verification: Solo noise layer → grit only; solo sub layer → pitched tone only
Changing sub WT does not alter noise distortion character
Combined blend is fuller than either layer alone
